item.title: Fujian coast guard conducts routine patrols in waters near Kinmen
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
BEIJING, Aug. 29 (Xinhua) -- The coast guard of east China's Fujian Province on Saturday conducted routine law-enforcement patrols in accordance with the law in the waters near Kinmen, a spokesperson with the China Coast Guard said. Zhu Anqing, the spokesperson, said the Fujian coast guard had dispatched task groups to strengthen control and management over relevant waters in August. "It is an effective step to protect the legitimate rights and interests, as well as the lives and property of fishermen on both sides of the Strait, and to ensure orderly navigation and activities in the waters between Xiamen and Kinmen," Zhu said.

item.title: Xi extends condolences over mudslide disaster in Nepal
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday sent a message of condolences to Nepali President Ram Chandra Poudel over a mudslide disaster that hit Nepal recently. In his message, Xi noted that a severe mudslide disaster occurred recently at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing between China and Nepal, causing heavy casualties, leaving people missing and resulting in property losses. On behalf of the Chinese government and people, Xi expressed deep condolences to the victims and sincere sympathies to the bereaved families, the injured and people in the disaster-stricken areas. Xi noted that China is making every effort to search for and rescue missing persons, relocate and resettle affected people, provide prompt medical treatment to the injured, minimize casualties and prevent secondary disasters. China and Nepal, Xi said, are connected by mountains and rivers and share a common destiny, adding that China is ready to actively assist Nepal in its rescue efforts and provide support and assistance to the best of its capability. Xi also expressed his belief that both peoples will be able to work together to overcome the disaster and rebuild their homes as soon as possible. On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang sent a message of condolences to Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

item.title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting on Gyirong County mudslide rescue efforts
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Friday chaired a Party leadership meeting to deliberate and make arrangements on rescue and relief efforts after a devastating mudslide hit Gyirong County in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. At the beginning of the meeting, Xi, who is also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, and other leaders observed a moment of silence to mourn the victims of the disaster, which struck the border port of Gyirong on Wednesday.

item.title: China urges Japan to accelerate disposal of abandoned chemical weapons
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
Gas masks produced by the Japanese military in China during WWII are displayed at the Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo, Changchun City, northeast China's Jilin Province, February 27, 2025. /VCG China on Friday urged the Japanese government to speed up the disposal of abandoned chemical weapons left in China from World War II. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a question about a recent exhibition on Japanese military poison gas held by a civil group in Yokohama, Japan. The exhibition showcased how the Japanese military produced poison gas and chemical weapons during World War II and used them in China and other Southeast Asian countries. Lin said Japanese militarism openly violated international law during World War II by developing chemical weapons on a large scale and using them in China and other Asian countries, bringing severe suffering and disasters to people across the region. Equipment used by the Japanese military to produce chemical weapons in China is displayed at the Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo, February 27, 2025. /VCG "After its defeat, Japan left behind a large number of chemical weapons in China in an attempt to cover up its crimes," Lin said, adding that these abandoned weapons have caused casualties among more than 2,000 people to date and posed serious threats to people's lives, safety and the ecological environment in China. Lin urged the Japanese government to fulfill its obligations, heed calls from Japanese people with a sense of justice and neighboring countries that suffered from the wartime atrocities, and fully and faithfully implement the relevant international conventions and the memorandum between the Chinese and Japanese governments. He called on Japan to accelerate the disposal process of abandoned chemical weapons and return a safe and clean environment to the Chinese people at an early date.

item.title: 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum to Be Held from Sept. 15 to 17: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- The 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum will be held from September 15 to 17, 2026, at Beijing International Convention Center,said Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press briefing on Thursday. Under the theme "Build Consensus on Stability, Advance Security Governance Together", this year's forum will feature four plenary sessions on International Order and Strategic Stability, Localized Conflicts: Predicaments and Pathways to Resolution, Risks and Challenges to Security and Stability in the Asia-Pacific, and The Role and Vision of Developing Countries. In addition, this forum will hold eight parallel sessions including Major-country Relations and Strategic Stability, Asian Approaches to Addressing Security Challenges, Sea Lane Security and Maritime Security Governance, Risks and Regulation of Military Applications of Emerging Technologies, and Trends in Outer Space Security Governance. "The 4th China-Africa Peace and Security Forum will also be convened in conjunction with the Xiangshan Forum," the spokesperson added. According to the spokesperson, the Beijing Xiangshan Forum will celebrate its 20th anniversary this year. Guided by the spirit of equality, openness, inclusiveness and mutual learning, the forum has evolved from a Track 2 exchange among defense think tanks into a major Track 1.5 platform for international security and defense dialogue. It serves to build consensus, deepen trust, and advance cooperation in global security governance and fostering a community with a shared future for humanity. "We invite defense and military leaders, representatives of international organizations, and renowned scholars to join the forum as we mark its 20th anniversary and explore solutions to global security governance together," said the spokesperson.
